title: Project Epsilon
summary: Self-built Linux privesc lab: a leftover backup file leads to the database, SSH and a sudo shell escape.

card.caption: The exploit path changes no files, cron jobs, services or database rows.

kpis.label: files, cron jobs, services or database rows changed by the exploit path
critical finding on the path to root

setup: An Azure VM running Apache, MariaDB and OpenSSH, reachable by solvers over WireGuard.

I wrote both the lab configuration and the solve write-up. The lab is built to stay stable for many solvers at once: no brute force, and the exploit path changes no files, cron jobs, services or database rows.
did: A leftover backup file leaks database credentials, the database leaks an SSH login, and a narrowly scoped sudo rule on `less` allows a shell escape to root. The write-up has a findings table: 1 critical, 2 high, 1 low.
results: A backup file left in the webroot and sudo rights on an interactive binary (less) opened a path to root.
next: Remove backup files from production servers and restrict sudo by least privilege.

signal: auditd execve of /bin/sh with parent process less
